prompt: Which correctly runs a task on a thread pool and waits for completion?
choices: Thread t = new Thread(() -> task()); t.run(); t.join();
ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4); pool.submit(() -> task()); pool.shutdown(); pool.awaitTermination(1, TimeUnit.MINUTES);
explanation: Submit to the pool, call shutdown() to stop accepting new tasks, then awaitTermination() to block until all submitted tasks finish. Option A calls run() (not start()) so no new thread is created. Option C uses sleep() — a fixed wait that may be too short or too long. Option D: wait() is an Object monitor method, not CompletableFuture.get().
